audience.programmeDescription: Criminology at Leiden studies crime, its causes and consequences, and the ways society responds to it. The programme combines legal, psychological and sociological perspectives with qualitative, quantitative and experimental research. Students examine offenders, victims, prevention, policing and criminal justice.
audience.comparisonExplanation: A complete UCR comparison is not yet available because the remaining compulsory third-year curriculum has not been established for the revised programme. The confirmed first two years and 30 EC of elective space are shown below. This incomplete external curriculum does not establish that UCR offers no suitable study possibilities.

curriculum.limitation: The first two years contain 24 compulsory courses totalling 120 EC. Together with 30 EC of third-year elective space, the listed components total 150 EC. The remaining 30 EC of compulsory third-year study, including the thesis, require confirmation for the revised curriculum. First-year tutoring and a Dutch criminological language test are additional zero-credit obligations. This is an incomplete curriculum, not a certified 180-EC degree plan.

componentNotes.y1-criminal-law: A compulsory first-year course. First-year Criminology students are registered for the programme’s courses by the university.
componentNotes.y2-quantitative-research-2: Builds on Quantitative Criminological Research 1; successful completion of that course is recommended before participation.
componentNotes.y2-qualitative-research-2: Develops qualitative analysis of secondary data and coding. The first-year research courses provide the preparatory foundation.
componentNotes.y3-open-electives: 30 EC of elective space. Choices must meet the applicable level, approval and non-overlap rules. Honours College courses do not count here; the Criminology minor cannot be used as a whole where it overlaps with compulsory study.
